proof_summary: Counting pairs divisible by each power of \(p\) and applying Legendre’s formula gives \(v_p(\mathrm{num}(N))=\sum_{i\ge1}\lfloor N/p^i\rfloor^2\) and \(v_p(\mathrm{den}(N))=\sum_{i\ge1}\sum_{r\le \lfloor N/p^i\rfloor} r\lfloor \lfloor N/p^i\rfloor/r\rfloor\); the bound on each inner sum by the corresponding square also proves the quotient is integral. For \(0\le k<p\), every \(\lfloor(np+k)/p^i\rfloor\) with \(i\ge1\) equals \(\lfloor np/p^i\rfloor\), so both valuations—and hence their difference—are constant across the block.
